summary: [para 3] 3. Vide Record of Proceedings for the hearing dated 6.5.2026, the Petitioner was directed to submit the information and clarification regarding (i) Special Audited Balance Sheet, duly supported by an Auditor’s certificate/ report, along with the income statement, schedules, and notes to accounts forming an integral part thereof, prepared in accordance with the Companies Act, 2013 and in compliance with Clause 3(b) of the Trading Licence Regulations, 2020, as on a date within 30 days preceding the date of the application, and to demonstrate compliance with net worth and the current and liquidity ratios for grant of a Category III Trading Licence, including complete particulars of loans, advances, and investments in associates and the related parties, and (ii) Clarify that the professionals, whose profiles have been submitted by the Petitioner, are engaged on a full-time basis, in compliance with Regulation 3(2) of the Trading Licence Regulations, 2020. [para 8] 8. The Petitioner has uploaded the application for the grant of a trading licence on its website in terms of Clause (3) of Regulation 6 of the Trading Licence Regulations, 2020, and further placed on record the relevant copies of the newspapers in original in which notice of its application has been published. As per Regulation 6(3) of the Trading Licence Regulations, 2020, the Petitioner was required to publish notices of its application within 7 days of filing, in two daily newspapers with circulation in each of the five regions, in addition to publications from Delhi, including one economic daily. The Petitioner, vide affidavit dated 31.3.2026, has submitted that notices under subsection (2) of Section 15 of the Act [¶] read with Clause (4) of Regulation 6 of the Trading Licence Regulations have been published by the Petitioner company on 10.4.2026 in all India edition of the ‘Business Standard’ (Kolkata, Chennai, New Delhi, Lucknow, and Mumbai), ‘Financial Express’ (New Delhi, Chennai/Kochi, Kolkata, Lucknow), ‘The North East Times’ (Guwahati) and ‘The Assam Rising’ (Guwahati). The Petitioner has submitted that no objection has been received in response to the public notices. [para 10] 10. In view of the above, it has been submitted by the Petitioner that it fulfils the requirements specified in Clause (1) of Regulation 3 of the Trading Licence Regulations. [para 17] 17. The Commission, upon perusal of the submissions and Audited Special Balance Sheet as on 28.2.2026, observed that although the Petitioner does not fulfil the liquidity ratio requirement, as stipulated under the applicable Regulations, the Petitioner possesses a net worth of ₹ 4,85,330 lakh, which is several times higher than the minimum net worth required for a Category-III trading licence. The Petitioner meets other criteria for the grant of a trading licence as required under the Trading [¶] the Petitioner, the Commission, in exercise of its powers under Regulation 23 of the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Procedure, Terms and Conditions for grant of Trading Licence and other related matters) Regulations, 2020, hereby [para 18] 18. In accordance with Clause (2) of Regulation 3 of the Trading Licence Regulations, the Petitioner should have at least one full-time professional possessing qualifications and experience in power system operation and the commercial aspects of power transfer, including finance, commerce and accounts.
